subChunks.title: RESTful API Design Principles

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: REST is the language of the internet. Your API is a contract — break it carelessly and every client that relies on it breaks too. Design it thoughtfully before you write a line of code.
A common mistake: using verbs in URLs. /api/createOrder is wrong. The verb is in the HTTP method. POST /api/orders is right.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Given these poorly designed endpoints, rewrite them following REST conventions. Print corrected lines.
guidedPractice.hint: GET /api/users/3, DELETE /api/users/5, POST /api/products — use nouns + HTTP methods.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the key REST constraints. What HTTP status code would you return when a resource is not found?

questions.prompt: Which HTTP method should be used to partially update a resource?
questions.explanation: PATCH applies a partial update. PUT replaces the entire resource.

questions.prompt: A client sends a POST to create a user and the user already exists. What HTTP status code should the API return?
options: 409 Conflict — indicates the request conflicts with the current state of the resource
questions.answer: 409 Conflict — indicates the request conflicts with the current state of the resource
questions.explanation: 409 signals a duplicate/conflict. 400 is for malformed requests. 422 is for semantically invalid input.

subChunks.title: @RestController & Request Mappings

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: @RestController is the gateway spell. Every request enters here, gets unpacked from JSON, routed to the right method, and the result is packed back into JSON for the client.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Write a simple controller simulation: a class with a getUser(long id) method that returns "User: " + id, and a createUser(String name) method returning "Created: " + name. Call both from main.
guidedPractice.hint: getUser returns "User: " + id. createUser returns "Created: " + name.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: What is the difference between @Controller and @RestController? What does @ResponseBody do?

questions.prompt: How do you extract a value from the URL path in Spring MVC?
questions.explanation: @PathVariable binds URI template variables. @RequestParam binds query string parameters.

subChunks.title: Validation, DTOs & Global Error Handling

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Never trust client input. The @Valid annotation is your first ward against chaos — it rejects malformed requests before they reach your business logic. Your GlobalExceptionHandler is the fallback ward.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Implement a validate(String username, String email) method: return "OK" if username is non-empty and email contains "@"; otherwise return "INVALID".

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Why use DTOs instead of passing domain entities directly to/from API endpoints?

questions.prompt: What annotation triggers Bean Validation on a @RequestBody parameter?
questions.explanation: @Valid triggers JSR-380 constraint validation on the annotated parameter. Spring returns 400 if constraints fail.

subChunks.title: API Security & Documentation

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: A public API without authentication is an unlocked treasury. JWT tokens are like signet rings — they prove who you are without requiring a stateful session on the server.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate JWT structure: a token has format header.payload.signature. Write extractPayload(String token) that splits on "." and returns the middle part.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain JWT authentication flow. Why do REST APIs use stateless token auth rather than server-side sessions?

questions.prompt: Why is CSRF protection typically disabled for REST APIs using JWT?
options: JWT is sent in the Authorization header, not a cookie, so CSRF attacks don't apply
JWT is more secure than CSRF tokens
REST APIs don't have forms to submit
CSRF protection slows down API calls
questions.answer: JWT is sent in the Authorization header, not a cookie, so CSRF attacks don't apply
questions.explanation: CSRF exploits browser cookie auto-attachment. JWTs in Authorization headers are not auto-sent by browsers, so CSRF is not a threat.
